bac3.supports: reported integration and germline transmission rate

bac4.quote: BAC transgenics faithfully recapitulate the endogenous gene expression patterns and allow for the estimation of the endogenous gene expression levels
bac4.supports: BAC reporters reported to follow endogenous patterns (which genes and tissues: unread)

bac5.quote: the genomic DNA piece in the BAC construct needs to be flanked by Tol2 transposon sites
bac5.supports: the BAC needs Tol2 sites to integrate: a carrier plus transposon, not an independent chromosome

ep1.quote: The epigenetic signatures also reveal many novel regeneration-specific enhancers, which are experimentally validated.
ep1.supports: regeneration-specific enhancers reported and validated in the fin

ep2.quote: regeneration enhancers are preset as hypomethylated before injury
ep2.supports: enhancers are hypomethylated before injury (bulk/sorted cells, not single-cell)

ep3.quote: We identified Fra1 (gene name: fosl1a), whose motif enrichment was top ranked, as a putative upstream transcription factor for fin regeneration
ep3.supports: fosl1a as a putative upstream TF from motif enrichment: an inference

ep4.supports: a fosl1a mutant genotype was analysed

ep5.quote: showed delayed regeneration after fin amputation compared to their wildtype littermates
ep5.supports: the mutant showed delayed fin regeneration: a causal perturbation, whole-fin, not cell-type-resolved

ep6.quote: expression activation of hoxc13a, lef1, and col1a1a co-occur with their promoters gaining chromatin accessibility
ep6.supports: lef1 expression rises with promoter accessibility: a measured correlation

ep7.quote: We took advantage of Tg(sp7:EGFP) stable lines, which express EGFP in differentiating and mature osteoblasts
ep7.supports: sp7:EGFP is a labelling/sorting strain for osteoblasts, not evidence that sp7 drives anything

gr1.quote: We identified and in vivo validated cell-type-specific and position-specific regeneration-responsive enhancers
gr1.supports: regeneration-responsive enhancers validated in vivo (F0 reporter) in adult regenerating fin

gr2.quote: paired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq on uninjured and regenerating fins
gr2.supports: assay and tissue of the regulatory map

gr3.quote: a marked increase in the accessibility of chromatin regions associated with regenerative and developmental processes at 1 dpa, followed by a gradual closure across major cell types at later stages
gr3.supports: accessibility peaks at 1 dpa then closes; 'developmental processes' here names gene annotations, not a developmental fin assay

gr4.quote: specific transcription factors (TFs) including fosl1a and vdra are essential in orchestrating the regenerative response
gr4.supports: the paper calls fosl1a an essential TF, as background citing earlier work; not a result of this paper

gr5.quote: cell-type-specific TFs with known function ranked at top by degree centrality, such as lef1 in BE, runx2a in MES, and spi1 in HEM
gr5.supports: lef1 ranked as a TF in basal epithelium by GRN degree centrality: an inference

gr6.quote: MES4 and MES5, with higher expression of col10a1a, sp7, ifitm5, bglap, and spp1, were maturing osteoblasts and osteocytes
gr6.supports: sp7 listed as a marker of maturing osteoblast/osteocyte clusters

gr7.supports: cldni and fras1 named as basal-epithelial markers

gr8.supports: msx1b and prrx1b named as mesenchymal markers

hac2.quote: Delivery to mammalian cells is streamlined by employing yeast spheroplast fusion
hac2.supports: HAC delivery is a distinct step from the construct: yeast spheroplast fusion into mammalian cells

hac3.quote: Harnessing centromere epigenetics permits human artificial chromosome (HAC) formation but is not sufficient to avoid rampant multimerization
hac3.supports: HAC formation uses epigenetic centromeres; multimerization is a failure mode (human cells)

ki1.quote: Targeting of ascl1b, olig2 and neurod1 resulted in 58%, 48% and 37%, respectively, of F0 injected embryos showing EGFP expression in the lens
ki1.supports: F0 secondary-marker rates for three neural loci

ki3.supports: the donor carries short (48 bp) homology arms

len1.quote: We next examined whether an isolated 1.3 kb sequence that corresponded to the H3K27ac-rich region could activate gene expression when fused to P2, which ostensibly includes the lepb promoter
len1.supports: LEN is an isolated 1.3 kb sequence tested fused to the lepb 2 kb promoter (P2)

len2.quote: fin amputation and ventricular resection activated eGFP fluorescence in blastemal and endocardial cells, respectively, in a similar manner to the lepb BAC sequences
len2.supports: an observation about the P7/LEN-P2 reporter lines (blastemal after fin amputation); not a cell-type specificity claim for LEN

len3.quote: Two regions within the lepb BAC, located 7 kb and 3 kb upstream of the lepb start codon, were enriched with H3K27ac marks in regenerating, but not uninjured, samples
len3.supports: location of the H3K27ac-marked regions relative to lepb

len4.quote: more distal LEN fragments composed of nucleotides 1–850, 450–1000, 450–850, or 660–850 could each drive eGFP expression from the lepb 2 kb promoter during fin regeneration
len4.supports: named LEN fragments drove eGFP from the lepb 2 kb promoter in regenerating fin

len5.quote: a small intergenic element we now refer to as lepb-linked enhancer, or LEN
len5.supports: the source's own name for the element

len6.quote: Upon fin amputation, lepb:eGFP fluorescence was sharply induced in regenerating structures, where fluorescence localized to blastemal mesenchyme
len6.supports: an observation about the lepb:eGFP BAC reporter, not about LEN

lepb.quote: Epigenetic profiling identified a short DNA sequence element upstream and distal to lepb that acquires open chromatin marks during regeneration and enables injury-dependent expression from minimal promoters.
lepb.supports: a regeneration-activated element drives injury-dependent expression from minimal promoters (zebrafish fin and heart)

modules.quote: was divisible into tissue-specific modules sufficient for expression in regenerating zebrafish fins or hearts
modules.supports: the element splits into fin-sufficient and heart-sufficient modules

pc1.quote: We found that the fos minimal promoter and Drosophila synthetic core promoter (DSCP) yielded high rates of leaky expression
pc1.supports: two minimal promoters leak in zebrafish enhancer assays

pc2.quote: drove little or no ectopic expression
pc2.supports: E1b, lepb P0.8, lepb P2 and ZSP promoters drove little or no ectopic expression

pc3.quote: We also found significant differences in compatibility among specific combinations of promoters and enhancers
pc3.supports: promoter choice changes enhancer output; compatibility must be tested per pair

pc4.quote: We observed limited basal activity for LEN-E1b, LEN-P0.8, and LEN-P2, as no larvae expressed EGFP in the heart, eye, or fin fold (n=227, 234, and 402, respectively)
pc4.supports: the leak assay scored three tissues (heart, eye, fin fold) in uninjured LARVAE; adult fin was not scored

pc5.quote: A total of 2%, 2%, and 61% of LEN-fos larvae expressed EGFP in the heart, eye, and tail fin fold, respectively (n=85)
pc5.supports: a leaky promoter lights up the larval fin fold (61%) even with a regeneration-only enhancer

pc6.quote: While ZSP alone directed expression in 19% of injured fin folds
pc6.supports: a promoter alone can express in injured larval fin fold, so an enhancer-less control is required

pc7.quote: 103runx1EN directs expression in the notochord and CNS of uninjured developing larvae and in the heart and fin in response to injury, indicating that it can function as either a developmental or regeneration enhancer
pc7.supports: developmental versus regeneration activity of one enhancer in larvae (as described in this paper, citing earlier work)

pc8.quote: gata2a-i4 is an evolutionarily conserved enhancer that regulates the developmental expression of gata2a in endothelial cells
pc8.supports: a developmental enhancer used as a comparator (endothelial; not a fin enhancer)

pc9.quote: Uninjured and 2 days post-amputation (dpa) adult F0 E1b:EGFP, LEN-E1b:EGFP, P2:EGFP, and LEN-P2:EGFP caudal fins.

pig1.supports: site-specific attP landing sites with reported germline transmission

pig2.quote: Transgenesis into these sites enables reproducible expression patterns in F0 zebrafish embryos for enhancer discovery
pig2.supports: landing-site integration reduces position variability for F0 enhancer tests (embryos)

tol1.quote: difficulties associated with defining and cloning a complete promoter and associated regulatory elements, combined with multicopy transgene integration, position effects and gene silencing

treeclasses.supports: authors' SUSPICION, not a result: development-and-injury elements

causal_gaps: Reporter activity shows that an element can drive expression in the tested context; it does not show that the element controls outgrowth, ECM deposition, ray geometry or fin stiffness.

The developmental-fin versus regeneration gap, scoped to the fish-fin trait bridge: PMC10211259 tests both developmental and regeneration enhancers in larval tissues, but no source read shows that any enhancer drives expression in the developing paired fin, or ties any enhancer to fin shape or stiffness.
Replicate independence of the multiome data is unconfirmed (metadata audit 1b77f81).
LEN coordinates and sequence are null: they were not read.

cell_context_and_stage.cell_programs: as listed in the regulatory map rows: basal epithelium, surface epithelium, fibroblast/mesenchyme, osteoblast and joint
cell_context_and_stage.stage: uninjured control and 1, 2, 4, 6 days post amputation (the sampled times of the multiome map)

cell_program_binding.binding_basis: root proposal: the map's mesenchymal program is the nearest named program to the blastemal observations; not established

designs.cell_specificity_inferred: none. The sources report blastemal fluorescence for lepb-region reporter lines (len2) and blastemal mesenchyme for the lepb:eGFP BAC reporter (len6); these describe those reporters, not LEN's cell-type specificity.
designs.cell_stage_specificity: Stage specificity read: regenerating adult fin at 0/1/2/4/6 dpa for the maps; the promoter-leak assays used LARVAE (heart, eye, fin fold). Adult-fin leak is unassessed. Cell-stage specificity of any chosen element is unknown until its own reporter is read by cell program.

minimal_promoter.alternatives_note: E1b, P0.8 and P2 showed no leak in uninjured larvae (pc4); adult-fin performance of LEN with E1b, P0.8 or ZSP was not read. fos and DSCP leaked (pc1, pc5) and are avoided.
minimal_promoter.name: lepb 2 kb promoter (P2)
minimal_promoter.pair_compatibility: differs by enhancer and promoter pair (pc3) and is NOT known for any untested pair
minimal_promoter.reason: the TREE paper fused LEN to P2; PMC10211259 names LEN-P2:EGFP in adult F0 caudal fin

implementation.carrier: circular Tol2 donor plasmid (enhancer, minimal promoter, reporter between Tol2 ends)
implementation.delivery: microinjection of the plasmid with transposase mRNA into one-cell embryos (injection step documented for the BAC variant in the abstract of the BAC protocol; plasmid-specific injection parameters were not read)
implementation.integration: transposase-mediated, random; copy number and position effects expected (knock-in paper's description of the Tol2 limits)
implementation.integration_alternative: a phiC31 attP landing site (pIGLET14a or pIGLET24b) would replace random Tol2 integration and fix the insertion site; this was read from the abstract only (pig1, pig2), the fin behaviour of such lines is unread
